findings.claim: configure-020d2-required-check.sh does not validate SCP_REQUIRED_CONTEXT before interpolating it into the heredoc PUT body at line 87. findings.evidence: configure-020d2-required-check.sh line 41: `REQUIRED_CONTEXT="${SCP_REQUIRED_CONTEXT:-policy-check / scp/policy-check}"` — no validation block follows. Lines 83–105: heredoc JSON contains `"contexts": ["${REQUIRED_CONTEXT}"]` (line 87); REQUIRED_CONTEXT is expanded in the heredoc at shell evaluation time, not escaped by jq. A value containing a double-quote closes the JSON string early (e.g., `foo" }` yields `"contexts": ["foo" }"...`), producing malformed JSON that the GitHub API rejects. A crafted value of the form `x"], "enforce_admins": false, "required_status_checks": {"strict": true, "contexts": ["x` would attempt to inject a duplicate `enforce_admins: false` field before the canonical `enforce_admins: true` on line 89; whether GitHub's parser honours the first or last instance of a duplicate key determines whether the gate is bypassed. Contrast: enable-required-check.sh lines 233–241 contains the validation block added in fix-round-3. configure-020d2-required-check.sh has no such block.
findings.impact: Malformed JSON scenarios safe-fail (gh exits non-zero; set -e aborts). The residual risk is a crafted duplicate-key injection that passes JSON parsing and causes GitHub to honour an attacker-controlled value for enforce_admins or contexts. This requires operator-level access to the execution environment (ability to set SCP_REQUIRED_CONTEXT). The gate-relevant field is enforce_admins: an injected false value would disable admin enforcement without the --i-understand-this-bypasses-the-gate friction path required by enable-required-check.sh. Probability: low (operator-level prerequisite). Consequence: enforcement gap on the SCP self-repo policy gate. The primary risk is inconsistency: R3 established that validation is required; 020D2 is now silently out of conformance with its own sister script.
findings.mitigation: Add the following validation block to configure-020d2-required-check.sh immediately after line 41 (the REQUIRED_CONTEXT assignment): `case "$REQUIRED_CONTEXT" in *'\`'*|*$'\n'*|*$'\r'*) echo "error: SCP_REQUIRED_CONTEXT contains markdown-corrupting chars (backtick, CR, LF)" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac; if [ "${#REQUIRED_CONTEXT}" -gt 200 ]; then echo "error: SCP_REQUIRED_CONTEXT is ${#REQUIRED_CONTEXT} chars; max 200" >&2; exit 1; fi`. This mirrors enable-required-check.sh lines 233–241 exactly, closing the asymmetry. Optionally also reject double-quote (`*'"'*`) to directly block heredoc JSON injection, though the LF/CR/backtick set is the minimal R3-established standard.

findings.impact: Not a bypass — exits non-zero. Operator diagnostic quality is reduced: on PUT failure the operator sees gh output with no script-level context identifying which step failed or what partial state to expect. Operationally inconsistent with the SAF-R3-003 POST fix applied one level up in the same function.
findings.mitigation: Wrap the PUT call in an explicit failure handler: `gh api -X PUT ... >/dev/null || { echo "[020D2] ERROR: unified PUT failed; required_signatures POST was not reached; no protection changes applied" >&2; exit 1; }`. Not a blocking merge issue.

r3_closure_verification.note: enable-required-check.sh line 365: `FAIL="${FAIL:-0}"` — the default-preserving initialisation is present and correctly positioned. Verified no-FAIL-write path between apply-phase (lines 329–348) and line 365: lines 352–364 are exclusively the verify-section GET (`AFTER_JSON`) and four jq extractions (`CHECKS_STRICT`, `CHECKS_CONTEXTS`, `APPLIED_ADMINS`, `SIGS_ENABLED`). None assign to FAIL. APPLY_FAIL=1 at line 334 (PUT failure) → FAIL=1 at line 339; or APPLY_FAIL=1 at line 342 (POST failure) → FAIL=1 at line 347. Both are preserved intact by `${FAIL:-0}` at line 365. The false-success laundering window introduced by fix-round-2 is closed. CLOSED.

enable-required-check.sh lines 233–241: case statement `*'\`'*|*$'\n'*|*$'\r'*)` rejects any REQUIRED_CONTEXT value containing a backtick, LF, or CR; `[ "${#REQUIRED_CONTEXT}" -gt 200 ]` applies 200-char cap. Evidence from probe-2 analysis confirms: LF/CR rejection prevents ~~~ outer-fence-close injection (a newline is required to open a line starting with `~~~`); backtick rejection prevents inline code-span corruption; jq `--arg` encodes REQUIRED_CONTEXT for the payload (no injection surface there); `grep -q -F` is fixed-string (no regex injection). Square brackets, parens, and hyphens cannot close a fenced block and are correctly not rejected. Validation set is correct and minimal. CLOSED.

configure-020d2-required-check.sh lines 118–122: POST is wrapped in `if ! gh api -X POST ... >/dev/null; then echo "ERROR: required_signatures POST failed; status-checks/admins/reviews are set but signatures are NOT" >&2; echo "partial branch-protection state on ${REPO}@${DEFAULT_BRANCH}; re-run after fixing PAT scope" >&2; exit 1; fi`. Explicit error message names the partial state and advises the operator to re-run. Asymmetric diagnostic quality vs bare set-e is resolved for the POST. CLOSED.

structured_review.summary: All three R3 safety findings confirmed closed: SAF-R3-001 (FAIL preservation) closed via `FAIL="${FAIL:-0}"` at line 365 with verified no-write gap in lines 352–364; SAF-R3-002 (REQUIRED_CONTEXT injection) closed via case-statement rejection of backtick/CR/LF + 200-char cap in enable-required-check.sh lines 233–241; SAF-R3-003 (020D2 POST diagnostic) closed via if-not wrapper at configure-020d2 lines 118–122. Fix-round-3 introduces one new MIN finding (SAF-R4-001): the REQUIRED_CONTEXT validation added to enable-required-check.sh was not applied symmetrically to configure-020d2-required-check.sh, which interpolates the same env-var directly into a heredoc JSON PUT body. The injection risk requires operator-level access and most payloads safe-fail as malformed JSON; the residual concern is a crafted duplicate-key injection that could set enforce_admins=false without the ack-flag friction path. Fix is one validation block mirroring lines 233–241. One new nit (SAF-R4-002): 020D2 PUT step has no custom diagnostic; fix-round-3 corrected the POST but not the PUT. Not a bypass; operator still sees gh CLI stderr and non-zero exit. Verdict: CONDITIONAL on SAF-R4-001. SAF-R4-002 is non-blocking. No new CRIT or MAJ surface from fix-round-3.
